mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points over three months signals labor market weakness, which negatively impacts consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate rise does not correlate with negative SPX returns in 6 out of 10 cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth, as measured by GDPC1, indicates strong economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth does not precede positive SPX returns in 7 out of 10 cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) is growing by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the joint condition does not precede positive SPX returns in 6 out of 10 cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in two consecutive months signals strong supply-side activity, which supports economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth does not correlate with positive SPX returns in 7 out of 10 cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 3% indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which lowers borrowing costs and stimulates investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are not positive in more than 50% of cases when FEDFUNDS < 3%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a year-over-year increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 5% signals inflationary pressures, which may lead to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL increases do not precede negative SPX returns in 6 out of 10 cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDP growth (GDPC1) is positive and housing starts (HOUST) are increasing, it signals strong demand-side activity, which supports economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the joint condition does not precede positive SPX returns in 7 out of 10 cases, the hypothesis is rejected.
